title: Transanal Rectal Recanalization Using a Temporary Intraluminal Stent Adapted from Sterile "Bogotá Bag" Material for Severe Anastomotic Rectal Stenosis in a Dog: A Case Report
content: Rectal stricture is uncommon in dogs but is a challenging sequela of inflammatory and surgical disorders of the large intestine, because mature cicatricial fibrosis limits the efficacy of conventional dilational techniques. This report describes a 9-year-old castrated male Siberian Husky that developed severe anastomotic rectal stenosis—a circumferential fibrotic ring with a residual lumen of approximately 3 × 2 mm—after resection of about 25 cm of rectum with end-to-end anastomosis complicated by anastomotic leakage. Clinical signs included tenesmus, dyschezia, and marked difficulty defecating, and the diagnosis was based on rectal palpation and abdominal imaging. Recanalization was performed through a completely transanal approach with electrosurgical release of the fibrotic tissue, followed by placement of a temporary intraluminal stent fashioned from sterile polyvinyl chloride obtained from a 0.9% sodium chloride bag, drawing on the temporary-support principle of the Bogotá bag. The stent maintained luminal patency during cicatricial remodeling and was removed at approximately one month without infection, hemorrhage, migration, or recurrent obstruction; functional defecation was preserved throughout approximately three months of follow-up. In this patient, transanal recanalization combined with a low-cost adapted intraluminal stent restored and maintained rectal patency.
